newsitem.title: USA: Philip Morris cites tobacco, U.S.food gains.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris cites tobacco, U.S.food gains.

text.p: Philip Morris Cos Inc, reporting higher 1996 fourth quarter earnings Wednesday, cited strong tobacco sales, both internationally and domestically, and good results from its domestic food operations.
The New York-based tobacco and food giant said its earnings gain stemmed in part from increased worldwide tobacco revenue of $8.71 billion, up 14.5 percent from $7.61 billion a year earlier.
Philip Morris said its international tobacco sales rose 19 percent in the quarter, to $5.50 billion. Domestic tobacco sales rose 7.4 percent, to $3.21 billion.
Domestic sales of Marlboro brand cigarettes, the best-selling brand in the world, were up 7.8 percent to 156.2 billion cigarettes in the quarter, the company said.
Philip Morris said its domestic food sales also added to the earnings growth.
For the quarter, domestic food sales adjusted for divestitures were up 0.4 percent to $7.0 billion.
Domestic food sales excluding the adjustment were down 0.9 percent to $7.06 billion.
Philip Morris said that during 1996 it repurchased 28.6 million shares of its common stock at a cost of $2.8 billion.
The company spent $2.1 billion to buy back its shares in 1995, a company spokesman said.
The spokesman said Philip Morris had "just under" $1 billion of buybacks to go in its $6 billion buyback program, launched in the fourth quarter of 1994.
Philip Morris shares were up 7/8 at 115-1/4 at midday.
